canonical_definition:
What it is. Across the available descriptions, papers treat KnowEdit as an integrated benchmark for evaluating knowledge editing methods. The benchmark is described as containing six datasets for different evaluation types, and one paper notes that experiments are conducted on the KnowEdit benchmark (Precise Localization of Memories: A Fine-grained Neuron-level Knowledge Editing Technique for LLMs).

What it is claimed to measure. Papers describe KnowEdit as evaluating knowledge editing methods across criteria such as success, portability, locality, and fluency. Beyond those benchmark criteria, no construct links or behavioral-indicator links are recorded, so the available usage does not connect it to a broader spread of named constructs.

Space of uses. The available paper uses KnowEdit as an experimental benchmark for assessing knowledge editing methods. No other measurement instruments are linked alongside it in the available relationships.
